name: The Hon. Justice Kettle
bio: Boils over slowly, then all at once. Believes every object deserves a fair hearing and a cup of tea.

name: Chief Justice Grandfather Clock
bio: Has presided since 1887. Punctual to the second. Deeply suspicious of anything with a snooze button.

name: Magistrate Rubber Duck
bio: Listens silently while defendants explain themselves, until they realise what they did wrong.

name: Malicious Disappearance
definition: Vanishing at the precise moment one is needed.
maximumSentence: Permanent relocation to a clearly labelled drawer

name: Premature Expiry
definition: Ceasing to function days after the warranty ends.
maximumSentence: Public display as a cautionary tale

name: Obtaining Trust by False Pretences
definition: Displaying a status (full bars, 'almost done', 'sunny') that is untrue.

name: Ambush of the Bare Foot
definition: Lying in wait on a floor, specifically in the dark.
maximumSentence: Confinement to a tub with a lid

name: Wilful Tangling
definition: Becoming knotted while left completely alone.

name: Disturbance of the Peace
definition: Beeping, creaking or rattling with no discernible purpose.

name: Conspiracy to Inconvenience
definition: Acting in concert with another object to ruin an afternoon.

name: The Left Sock
description: Last seen entering a washing machine in 2019. Its partner still waits in the drawer.

name: The Washing Machine
description: Suspected of running an underground sock-trafficking operation behind its door seal.

name: The Wi-Fi
description: Displays full bars while delivering nothing. Most active during video calls with your boss.

name: The Printer
description: Has not printed a document on the first try since its manufacture. Demands cyan to print in black.

name: The Lego Brick
description: A known ambusher. Operates exclusively at night on hallway floors.

name: Monday
description: Arrives every week without fail, despite repeated written objections.

name: The Alarm Clock
description: Believed to be in league with Monday. Its snooze button is widely considered entrapment.

name: Irish Weather
description: Forecast as 'sunny intervals'. Delivered horizontal rain in all four directions.

name: The Charging Cable
description: Charges only when held at a precise angle known to no living person.

name: The Headphones
description: Emerge from every pocket as a single solid knot, despite being put away neatly.

name: The Toaster
description: Settings 1 to 5 all produce either bread or charcoal. Nothing in between.

name: The Shopping Trolley
description: Steers only to the left. Refuses all correction. No relation to the Left Sock (denied).

title: The Disappearance on Laundry Day
testimony: I put in two socks. I took out one sock. I searched the drum, the door seal and the laundry basket. I checked the other sock. It had no explanation either.

sentence: Permanent relocation to a clearly labelled drawer, pending recapture.
judgeRemarks: The court notes that the defendant has never once been found. Absence is not innocence.

title: Accessory to Sock Disappearance
testimony: Every sock that has vanished was last seen inside this machine. It hums innocently. Too innocently.

sentence: Monthly inspection of its door seal by a qualified sock investigator.
judgeRemarks: Following the precedent in the Laundry Day matter, the machine is found to have provided the getaway vehicle.

title: Full Bars, Zero Internet
testimony: The defendant showed five full bars for the entire meeting. My face froze mid-sentence while presenting quarterly numbers. My boss saw me frozen with my mouth open for 40 seconds.

sentence: Mandatory honesty indicator: bars must now reflect actual performance.
judgeRemarks: Displaying full bars while delivering nothing is the purest form of false pretences this court has seen.

title: The Cyan Ransom
testimony: Deadline at 9am. Document is black and white. The printer refused to print because it was out of cyan. It then jammed, unjammed and printed a single blank page.

sentence: Removal of voice privileges and all error codes replaced with plain English.
judgeRemarks: As in the matter of Full Bars, Zero Internet, a device claiming readiness it cannot deliver is guilty. The court also finds it coordinated with the Wi-Fi to reject the print job twice.

title: The 3am Hallway Incident
testimony: I went to get a glass of water in the dark. I will not describe the sound I made. The defendant was exactly in the middle of the hallway, studs facing up.

sentence: Confinement to a tub with a lid, indefinitely.
judgeRemarks: The defendant did not speak in its defence. It did not need to. Studs facing up is intent.

title: Monday, Again
testimony: It came back. We told it not to. It came back anyway, and brought emails.

sentence: None. The court cannot sentence the passage of time.
judgeRemarks: Regrettably, Monday is operating within the calendar. The court is sympathetic, but its hands are literally tied to the calendar.

title: The Snooze Button Entrapment
testimony: The button says 'snooze'. It is the largest button on the device. It is right there. And then it gives me nine minutes. Nine! Who decided nine?

sentence: Probation until noon, and the snooze interval to be set to a round number.
judgeRemarks: Unlike Monday, the Alarm Clock chose its actions. Nine minutes is a deliberate cruelty.

title: Sunny Intervals (Alleged)
testimony: The forecast said sunny intervals. I got sun, hail, sideways rain and a rainbow in 25 minutes. I was wearing shorts.

sentence: None. The defendant technically delivered sunny intervals.
judgeRemarks: The court finds that 'intervals' was doing a great deal of work in that forecast. Case dismissed with a warning to bring a jacket.

title: Charging Only at 37 Degrees
testimony: It only charges if the cable is bent at a specific angle and the phone is not touched, looked at or thought about.

judgeRemarks: The court accepts it is old and tired. Still, 37 degrees is not a reasonable demand.

title: The Pocket Knot
testimony: I coiled them neatly. I put them in my pocket. I took them out 20 minutes later and they were a single solid sphere.

judgeRemarks: Tangling while completely unattended demonstrates independent criminal intent.

title: The Cable Tangle Syndicate
testimony: The day after the Pocket Knot, the charging cable was found knotted into the headphones. They were holding hands.

judgeRemarks: Given the Pocket Knot conviction, the court finds a pattern of coordinated tangling.

title: Setting Three Means Nothing
testimony: Setting 3 yesterday: warm bread. Setting 3 today: a fire alarm. The dial is decorative.

sentence: Mandatory honesty indicator on the dial.
judgeRemarks: Like the Wi-Fi, the dial promises one thing and delivers another. The court is lenient: the Toaster is a close colleague of the bench.

title: Veering Left in Aisle Four
testimony: It veered into the biscuits. Every time I corrected it, it screamed. The whole shop looked.

judgeRemarks: The court finds the defendant was drawn to the biscuits by forces understood by all present. Not guilty.

title: The Second Sock (Appeal Pending)
testimony: It happened again. Different socks. Same machine. I believe it's the same sock operating under an alias.

title: The Printer Strikes at 8:59
testimony: It made a grinding noise, displayed 'Error 0x8F', and died one minute before the board meeting.
